title: Assessment of airways, tremor and chronotropic responses to inhaled salbutamol in the quantification of beta 2-adrenoceptor blockade
authors: Lipworth BJ, Brown RA, McDevitt DG
population: Five healthy volunteers, single-blind crossover after oral atenolol 50, 100 or 200 mg, propranolol 40 mg or placebo, with cumulative inhaled salbutamol 200 to 6200 µg
funder: not read: PubMed Central holds only a scanned page image of the article.
result: Increasing doses of atenolol progressively reduced salbutamol-induced heart rate, finger tremor and airway conductance responses, and propranolol 40 mg attenuated them most; the attenuation was similar for heart rate, tremor and airway conductance. Geometric mean dose ratios against placebo for atenolol 50, 100 and 200 mg and propranolol 40 mg: heart rate 1.98, 2.75, 4.29 (none obtained for propranolol); tremor 1.60, 3.78, 6.34, 80.50; airway conductance 1.08, 4.35, 12.30, 66.0. The authors proposed the chronotropic response to inhaled salbutamol as a measure of beta2-adrenoceptor blockade.
